title: OOP & C++ MCQs
subject: cpp-oop
description: Practice MCQs on classes, inheritance, polymorphism, encapsulation, and STL for C-CAT preparation. Essential revision material for aspirants.

questions.question: Which OOP concept allows a derived class to provide a specific implementation of a method already defined in its base class?
questions.explanation: Method overriding lets a derived class redefine a base class method with the same signature, enabling runtime polymorphism.
Since show() is virtual, C++ resolves the call at runtime based on the actual object type (Derived), not the pointer type (Base) — this is dynamic dispatch.

questions.question: Which access specifier allows a class member to be accessed only within the same class and by derived classes, but not from outside?
questions.explanation: protected members are accessible within the declaring class and any derived class, but not from outside the class hierarchy.

questions.question: What is a pure virtual function in C++?
options: A function with no return type
A virtual function with a body but no declaration
A virtual function declared with '= 0' that has no implementation in the base class
A static function that cannot be overridden
questions.explanation: A pure virtual function is declared as 'virtual void func() = 0;' It has no implementation in the base class and forces derived classes to implement it, making the base class abstract.

questions.question: Which of these best describes constructor overloading?
options: Defining multiple constructors with the same name but different parameter lists
Calling a constructor from another constructor
A constructor that overrides a base class constructor
questions.explanation: Constructor overloading means a class can have multiple constructors, differentiated by their parameter lists, similar to function overloading.

questions.question: What happens if a base class destructor is NOT declared virtual, and a derived object is deleted through a base class pointer?
options: Only the base class destructor runs, causing a potential resource leak in the derived class
Only the derived class destructor runs
Both destructors run in the correct order regardless
questions.explanation: Without a virtual destructor, deleting a derived object via a base pointer only calls the base destructor, skipping the derived class's cleanup — a common source of memory/resource leaks.

questions.question: Which C++ feature allows the same operator to behave differently based on the operand types?
questions.explanation: Operator overloading lets you redefine how operators like +, -, or == behave for user-defined types (classes/structs).

questions.question: In C++, what does the 'friend' keyword allow?
options: A function or class outside the class to access its private and protected members
A class to inherit from multiple base classes
A function to be called without an object
A member function to be overridden
questions.explanation: A friend function or friend class is granted access to the private and protected members of the class that declares it as a friend, even though it isn't a member itself.

questions.question: Which type of inheritance can lead to the 'diamond problem' in C++?
questions.explanation: The diamond problem occurs in multiple inheritance when a class inherits from two classes that both inherit from a common base, creating ambiguity about which base copy to use — resolved in C++ using virtual inheritance.

questions.question: What is the primary purpose of C++ templates?
options: To enable generic programming with types as parameters
To enforce strict type checking at runtime
questions.explanation: Templates let you write functions and classes that work with any data type, with the actual type substituted at compile time — the foundation of generic programming in C++ (e.g. the STL).

questions.question: Which STL container stores elements in contiguous memory and provides fast random access via index?
questions.explanation: std::vector stores elements contiguously like a dynamic array, giving O(1) random access, unlike std::list (doubly linked list) which only allows sequential access.

questions.question: What does encapsulation in OOP primarily achieve?
options: Combining data and the methods that operate on it into a single unit, while restricting direct access to internal state
Allowing a class to have multiple forms
Reducing the number of classes needed
questions.explanation: Encapsulation bundles data (attributes) and behavior (methods) together within a class, and uses access specifiers to hide internal implementation details from outside code.
